title: N, P and K fertilization with agrinutri — DPI Emilia-Romagna 2026
text: vignette shows use agrinutri 0.6.0 compute full nitrogen, phosphorus potassium fertilisation plan following Disciplinari di Produzione Integrata (DPI) Emilia-Romagna 2026. package reproduces logic official regional tool Fert_Office v1.26 (Febbraio 2026, Regione Emilia-Romagna) makes scriptable R. package implements two complementary methods: Metodo del bilancio (Allegato 2): full nutrient mass balance crop demand, soil supply, losses, previous-crop effects organic contributions. Recommended detailed soil climate data available. Scheda dose Standard: simplified per-crop dose user-selectable decrement increment factors, capped MAS (Massimali Ammessi di Simulazione). Recommended soil analyses limited. package also provides fertilisation distribution plan end--cycle soil P K estimation close agronomic loop planning recording.

title: N, P and K fertilization with agrinutri — DPI Emilia-Romagna 2026
text: agrinutri mixes English Italian terminology design: Function names: English snake_case (e.g. N_balance, P_balance, plan_distribution, classify_pH). Three exceptions retain Italian DPI canonical name: scheda_N, scheda_PK, get_MAS / check_MAS. Parameters: English snake_case throughout. Class strings (e.g. “molto bassa”, “media”, “Sabbiosi”) kept Italian DPI canonical labels. Soil-group labels accepted three conventions: Italian plural (“Sabbiosi”, “Medio impasto”, “Argillosi e limosi”), Italian singular (“Sabbioso”, “Franco”, “Argilloso”) English (“Sandy textures”, “Loamy textures”, “Clay textures”). normalise_soil_group() helper canonicalises .
code: library(agrinutri) normalise_soil_group("Loamy textures") #> $id_rag #> [1] 2 #>  #> $it_plural #> [1] "Medio impasto" #>  #> $it_singular #> [1] "Franco" #>  #> $en #> [1] "Loamy textures" normalise_soil_group("Franco") #> $id_rag #> [1] 2 #>  #> $it_plural #> [1] "Medio impasto" #>  #> $it_singular #> [1] "Franco" #>  #> $en #> [1] "Loamy textures" resolve_id_rag(clay = 18.5, sand = 15.5) #> [1] 2

title: N, P and K fertilization with agrinutri — DPI Emilia-Romagna 2026
text: result matches Fert_Office Bilancio sheet: = 186.6, B = 73.84, D = 39.536 (includes |E| = 10), G = 10.05, N required ≈ 142.25 kg/ha.
code: n_bal <- N_balance(   expected_yield_tons_ha = yield,   crop = crop,   ccp  = "Spring-summer crop 100-130 days",   sand = sand, clay = clay,   Ntot = Ntot, SOM = SOM, CN = CN,   oxygen_availability = oxygen,   winter_rain = winter_rain,   start_spring_rain = start_spring_rain,   prev_crop = prev_crop,   source = "None",   fertorg_frequency = "every year",   location = location,   forg_quantity = 0,   soil_seeding = soil_seeding,   greenhouse = greenhouse,   E_to_D = TRUE        # fold negative E into D, as in foglio Bilancio )  n_bal #>       A     B b1    b2 C1 C2      D E F Forg     G G_deposition G_fixation #> 1 186.6 73.84 39 34.84  0  0 39.536 0 0    0 10.05        10.05          0 #>   no_till_reduction C_tempo N_pct N_limit surplus_pluviometrico #> 1                 0    0.67     1     340                 FALSE  # Final dose n_dose <- calculate_N_fertilization(n_bal) n_dose #> [1] 142.246 # Signed terms in N_fert = A - B + C1 + C2 + D - E - F - Forg - G (kg N/ha) signed <- c(   A = n_bal$A, B = -n_bal$B, C1 = n_bal$C1, C2 = n_bal$C2, D = n_bal$D,   E = -n_bal$E, F = -n_bal$F, Forg = -n_bal$Forg, G = -n_bal$G ) op <- par(mar = c(7, 4, 3, 1)) cols <- grDevices::hcl.colors(length(signed), "BluYl", alpha = 0.9) barplot(   as.numeric(signed), names.arg = names(signed), las = 2, col = cols,   border = NA, ylab = "kg N/ha",   main = "N balance terms (signed toward mineral N need)" ) abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray40") par(op)

what: Precision agriculture: variable-rate from balance + NDVI
title: N, P and K fertilization with agrinutri — DPI Emilia-Romagna 2026
text: agrinutri bridges agronomic balance (constant-rate dose, kg/ha) NDVI-based variable-rate application. integration logic : Compute field-average dose N_balance() + calculate_N_fertilization() scheda_N(). Use NDVI proxy crop vigour: low NDVI → N (rescue), high NDVI → less N (already vigorous). Apply one two agrinutri variable-rate algorithms: Calibration curve (estimate_N_rate_from_calibration_curve()): two-point three-point linear interpolation observed NDVI extremes user-defined N rates. Holland & Schepers (estimate_N_rate_from_holland_schepers()): sufficiency-index method using q95 NDVI reference base N rate. wrapper variable_rate_N() glues balance NDVI one call, preserves field-average dose rescaling (optionally) caps pixel MAS limit.

text: package implements Italian DPI Emilia-Romagna specification. Coefficients thresholds differ Italian regions national standards. plan_distribution() function checks totals vs balance targets ZVN 170 kg N/ha limit, yet check MAS per single application specific modality-cycle DPI constraints (cycle_modality.table). future release add checks. s2.rast dataset minimal Sentinel-2 NDVI raster used vignettes examples; production use, replace NDVI raster (Sentinel-2, drone, source) desired resolution. variable_rate_N() re-scales raster field-average matches agronomic dose; instead want allow mean drift (e.g. upper/lower envelopes explicitly chosen), use underlying estimate_N_rate_from_calibration_curve() / estimate_N_rate_from_holland_schepers() directly. crops multiple phases (e.g. grano duro fase nd), MAS lookup uses first matching row; pass phase = ... explicitly ambiguity matters.

title: Nitrogen Fertilization Management with agrinutri: A Comprehensive Guide
text: agrinutri R package provides comprehensive toolkit calculating nitrogen fertilization requirements field crops following Emilia-Romagna Regional Recommendations integrated production. vignette demonstrates use agrinutri nitrogen balance calculations, soil fertility assessment, precision agriculture applications.

title: Nitrogen Fertilization Management with agrinutri: A Comprehensive Guide
text: Nitrogen balance quantitative method accounts nitrogen inputs outputs agricultural system. general equation used agrinutri : Nitrogen Fertilization (N)=−B+C1+C2+D−E−Forg−G\text{Nitrogen Fertilization (N)} = - B + C1 + C2 + D - E - F_{org} - G : : Crop nitrogen requirements (kg/ha) B: Soil nitrogen supply (sum b1 b2) (kg/ha) C1: Nitrogen leaching loss winter (kg/ha) C2: Nitrogen leaching loss spring (kg/ha) D: Immobilization dispersion losses (kg/ha) E: Nitrogen previous crop residues (kg/ha) F_{org}: Nitrogen organic fertilizers (kg/ha) G: Natural nitrogen contributions (kg/ha)

title: Nitrogen Fertilization Management with agrinutri: A Comprehensive Guide
text: agrinutri implements method balance (Allegato 2) Disciplinari di Produzione Integrata (DPI) Emilia-Romagna, line Guida alla Fertilizzazione Minerale e Organica (DPI 2025) regional tool FertDPI / Fert_Office. References: DPI Norme Generali (Allegato 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9), Reg. reg. 2/2024 3/2017, Direttiva Nitrati (91/676/CEE). Zone Vulnerabili ai Nitrati (ZVN) MAS (limiti di massima applicazione standard) binding 170 kg N/ha/year ceiling livestock effluents applies farm level. Formula N (Guida DPI 2025): N da apportare = − B + C + D − E − F − G = Fabbisogni colturali (assorbimenti unitari × produzione attesa). B = Fertilità del suolo: B1 (mineralizzazione S.O.: coefficiente × S.O. % × coefficiente tempo) + B2 (azoto pronto: coefficiente × N totale ‰; solo colture con ciclo < 1 anno). Per pluriennali B = B1 soltanto. C = Perdite per lisciviazione: Ca (autunno-inverno: <150 mm nessuna; 150–250 mm perdita progressiva; >250 mm tutto l’N pronto) + Cb (febbraio: 1 kg N/ha ogni 10 mm oltre 250 mm cumulati). D = Immobilizzazione e dispersione = B × fattore di correzione fc (funzione di ossigeno e tessitura: es. buona 0,15–0,25, moderata 0,20–0,30, impedita 0,30–0,40). E = N da residui della precessione (tabella: cereali paglia asportata −10, interrata −30; medica +80; soia 0; leguminose da granella +40; ecc.). F = N da fertilizzazioni organiche anni precedenti (ammendanti 50/30/20 %; Cattle slurry 30/15/10; suino/pollina 15/10/5). G = Apporti naturali (precipitazioni; fissazione per leguminose). agrinutri computes balance subtracts current-year organic N (Forg) obtain mineral N apply. Fractioning rules (max 100 kg/ha N per intervention herbaceous crops, 60 kg/ha tree crops; min 7 days interventions) presemina/autumn caps (e.g. max 30 kg/ha presemina, max 40 kg/ha arboree 15 Oct) set DPI must respected field plan. Soil texture (DPI groupings): 12 USDA texture classes grouped three macro-categories used efficiency coefficients: (1) Tendenzialmente sabbioso (S, SF, FS), (2) Franco / Medio impasto (L, F, FL, FSA, FA), (3) Tendenzialmente argilloso (FLA, , AL, ). agrinutri’s tri3() calc_soil_group_and_id_rag() provide texture soil group. Maximum allowed doses (MAS): crop ceiling N P₂O₅ must exceeded. Use get_MAS(crop) check_MAS(crop, N_planned) retrieve check MAS (see section ). Organic N efficiency (DPI): share organic N available crop year application depends fertilizer type, distribution technique (efficient / medium / low), soil texture. Efficient = injection, fertigation, incorporation within 4 h; medium = band spreading quick incorporation; low = surface spreading without incorporation. Ammendanti compostati use fixed 40% efficiency. agrinutri’s organic_fertilization() uses factors source frequency; DPI-specific efficiency soil distribution, refer FertDPI ‘Efficienza’ sheet regional guide.

title: Nitrogen Fertilization Management with agrinutri: A Comprehensive Guide
text: agrinutri provides following categories functions: Field-scale nitrogen balance - N_balance() plus ten component helpers (crop demand, soil supply, leaching, immobilisation, previous-crop residue, organic contributions, natural deposition). Phosphorus potassium balance - P_balance(), K_balance(). Distribution plan - plan_distribution() MAS 170 kg N ZVN checks. Precision agriculture - variable_rate_N(), estimate_N_rate_from_calibration_curve() estimate_N_rate_from_holland_schepers() VI-based VRT; build_strip_prescription() machine-width strips along -B line; export_prescription() / export_prescription_all() Shapefile, GeoJSON, KML, GeoPackage, John Deere, Trimble ISOXML TASKDATA formats. Remote-sensing diagnosis - compute_vi() (six VIs), compute_NNI() / compute_NNI_from_S2() / crop_params_NNI() GPR-based pipeline, nni_from_vi_empirical() single-VI regression path, estimate_biophysical() canopy trait retrieval. Farm-level workflow - farm_balance() iterates N_balance() every feature GeoJSON / Shapefile returns enriched sf layer ready export. Shiny application - run_app() opens six-tab web interface interactive forms, leaflet maps one-click export.

code: # Create example NDVI raster set.seed(42) ndvi_raster <- terra::rast(nrows=20, ncols=20, xmin=0, xmax=100, ymin=0, ymax=100) terra::values(ndvi_raster) <- runif(terra::ncell(ndvi_raster), 0.35, 0.85)  # Two-point calibration n_rate_2pt <- estimate_N_rate_from_calibration_curve(   raster = ndvi_raster,   minN = 40,  # N rate for max NDVI (healthy areas)   maxN = 80,  # N rate for min NDVI (areas needing more N)   calibration_type = "two-point",   plot = FALSE )  # Three-point calibration (more accurate) n_rate_3pt <- estimate_N_rate_from_calibration_curve(   raster = ndvi_raster,   minN = 40,   meanN = 60,  # N rate for mean NDVI   maxN = 80,   calibration_type = "three-point",   plot = FALSE )  # Compare results cat("Two-point calibration - Mean N rate:",     round(terra::global(n_rate_2pt, "mean", na.rm=TRUE)[1,1], 2), "kg/ha\n") #> Two-point calibration - Mean N rate: 60.05 kg/ha cat("Three-point calibration - Mean N rate:",     round(terra::global(n_rate_3pt, "mean", na.rm=TRUE)[1,1], 2), "kg/ha\n") #> Three-point calibration - Mean N rate: 60.03 kg/ha  # Spatial maps: NDVI and recommended N rate (variable-rate prescription) op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE) par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(2, 2, 2.5, 1)) terra::plot(ndvi_raster, main = "NDVI (example)", axes = FALSE,              col = grDevices::hcl.colors(100, "Greens", rev = TRUE)) terra::plot(n_rate_2pt, main = "N rate — 2-point (kg/ha)", axes = FALSE,              col = grDevices::hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE)) terra::plot(n_rate_3pt, main = "N rate — 3-point (kg/ha)", axes = FALSE,              col = grDevices::hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE)) par(op)

what: 3. Strip prescription along an A-B line
title: Farm-level balance and strip-prescription map
text: build_strip_prescription() tiles one plot parallel strips user-supplied working width. -B line given, longest side field used driving direction. Dose variability can driven uniform target, VI calibration curve, NNI zones, quantile classes.  Swapping VI calibration curve makes dose decrease vigour; mean across field preserved (mass-balance constraint) default. 2-D grid (variable dose cell--cell) produced passing cell_length > 0; explicit -B direction set angle_deg (degrees, 0 = east, 90 = north) supplying sf LINESTRING ab_line:
code: field <- farm[1, ]          # Campo Grande, 5.2 ha silage maize  # Option A: uniform 226 kg N/ha (from the balance), 24 m spreader rx_uni <- build_strip_prescription(   field         = field,   machine_width = 24,   variability   = "uniform",   n_target      = 226)  plot(sf::st_geometry(rx_uni), col = "#D5E4F0",      border = "#1F4E79", main = "Uniform strips, 24 m") # Option B: VI calibration (requires an NDVI raster) rx_cal <- build_strip_prescription(   field         = field,   machine_width = 24,   variability   = "calibration",   vi_raster     = my_ndvi_raster,   n_target      = 226,   min_dose      = 80,  max_dose = 260,   vi_low        = 0.35, vi_high = 0.80) # Option C: 24 m working width x 50 m along-strip cells, AB = 30 deg rx_grid <- build_strip_prescription(   field         = field,   machine_width = 24,   cell_length   = 50,   angle_deg     = 30,   variability   = "classes",   vi_raster     = my_ndvi_raster,   n_target      = 226,   min_dose      = 80, max_dose = 260,   n_classes     = 5)  # Option D: NNI-driven zones rx_nni <- build_strip_prescription(   field         = field,   machine_width = 24,   cell_length   = 0,           # continuous strips   variability   = "nni",   nni_raster    = my_nni_map,   n_target      = 226,   min_dose      = 80, max_dose = 260,   thr_lo        = 0.90, thr_hi = 1.10)

title: Prescription map worked example: NDVI, calibration curve, grid
text: real workflow read GeoTIFF UAV Sentinel-2. build plausible NDVI one line using internal demo helper (synthesiser used Shiny “Load demo NDVI” button):
code: library(terra)  # Two-patch NDVI with smooth base + noise set.seed(7) fp <- sf::st_transform(field, 3857) bb <- sf::st_bbox(fp)  nx <- 150 ny <- 110 r  <- terra::rast(xmin = bb$xmin, xmax = bb$xmax,                   ymin = bb$ymin, ymax = bb$ymax,                   ncols = nx, nrows = ny, crs = "EPSG:3857")  x  <- seq(0, 1, length.out = nx); y <- seq(0, 1, length.out = ny) gx <- matrix(x, nrow = ny, ncol = nx, byrow = TRUE) gy <- matrix(y, nrow = ny, ncol = nx) base   <- 0.72 + 0.05 * sin(4 * gx) + 0.04 * cos(5 * gy) patch1 <- 0.22 * exp(-(((gx - 0.30)^2 + (gy - 0.35)^2) / 0.010)) patch2 <- 0.26 * exp(-(((gx - 0.70)^2 + (gy - 0.55)^2) / 0.008)) ndvi_vals <- base - patch1 - patch2 + 0.03 * rnorm(nx * ny) ndvi_vals <- pmin(pmax(ndvi_vals, 0.30), 0.92) terra::values(r) <- ndvi_vals r <- terra::mask(r, terra::vect(fp))  names(r) <- "NDVI" r #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 110, 150, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 3.116946, 4.010757  (x, y) #> extent      : 1082192, 1082660, 5629081, 5629522  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator (EPSG:3857) #> source(s)   : memory #> name        :     NDVI #> min value   : 0.383404 #> max value   : 0.901509  terra::plot(r, main = "Input NDVI (synthetic)",             col = hcl.colors(30, "YlGn"))

title: Prescription map worked example: NDVI, calibration curve, grid
text: two-point linear calibration maps NDVI reference (lowest vigour) max_dose (push canopy development) high-vigour NDVI min_dose (canopy already lush, less N needed):
code: # Agronomic N target from the field-scale balance (example: 220 kg N/ha # for an 11 t/ha grain maize in Pianura Padana) N_target <- 220 min_dose <- 60 max_dose <- 260  vi_low  <- 0.35    # anchor for max_dose vi_high <- 0.80    # anchor for min_dose  # Plot the calibration vi  <- seq(0.20, 0.95, length.out = 200) slope <- (min_dose - max_dose) / (vi_high - vi_low) intercept <- max_dose - slope * vi_low dose_curve <- pmin(pmax(slope * vi + intercept, min_dose), max_dose)  plot(vi, dose_curve, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#1F4E79",      xlab = "NDVI", ylab = "N rate (kg N/ha)",      main = "Two-point calibration curve") abline(v = c(vi_low, vi_high), lty = 3, col = "#888") abline(h = c(min_dose, max_dose), lty = 3, col = "#888") points(c(vi_low, vi_high), c(max_dose, min_dose),        pch = 19, col = "#C0392B") text(vi_low,  max_dose, sprintf("(NDVI=%.2f, N=%d)", vi_low, max_dose),      pos = 4, cex = 0.9, col = "#C0392B") text(vi_high, min_dose, sprintf("(NDVI=%.2f, N=%d)", vi_high, min_dose),      pos = 2, cex = 0.9, col = "#C0392B")

title: Prescription map worked example: NDVI, calibration curve, grid
text: variable_rate_N() applies calibration every pixel rescales output area-weighted mean equals balance target (mass-balance constraint). method = "calibration" two anchor points taken automatically empirical min / max NDVI raster mapped (maxN, minN) — .e. lowest-vigour pixels get highest dose vice-versa. need fix anchors (e.g. force vi_low = 0.35 vi_high = 0.80 local calibration), use Option B build_strip_prescription() , exposes arguments.  %||% just defensive code (versions variable_rate_N() return list, others raster directly); defined top vignette hidden setup chunk.
code: vr <- variable_rate_N(   ndvi_raster = r,   n_dose      = N_target,   method      = "calibration",      # or "holland" for Holland & Schepers   minN        = min_dose,   maxN        = max_dose )  rx_raster <- vr$rate_raster %||% vr    # robust to return shape terra::plot(rx_raster,             main = "VRT raster (kg N/ha)",             col = rev(hcl.colors(30, "RdYlGn"))) cat("Mean applied N:  ", round(terra::global(rx_raster, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1], 1),     "kg N/ha\n") #> Mean applied N:   220 kg N/ha cat("Range:           ", round(terra::global(rx_raster, "min", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1], 1),     "-", round(terra::global(rx_raster, "max", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1], 1), "kg N/ha\n") #> Range:            103.9 - 260 kg N/ha

text: pixel--pixel raster Option fine self-driving tractor continuous-rate spreader, many farm monitors prefer block prescription: rectangular cells machine_width x cell_length single dose per cell. agrinutri’s build_strip_prescription() produces exactly , applying calibration internally:  -B direction inferred longest edge field polygon. title: Prescription map worked example: NDVI, calibration curve, grid
text: Mass-balance constraint - preserve_mean = TRUE (default) makes area-weighted mean dose match n_target. balance provides legally defensible field ceiling (MAS / ZVN 170 kg N/ha), VRT / grid layer redistributes space. Calibration sources - default anchors (vi_low = 0.35, vi_high = 0.80) work mid-season Sentinel-2 NDVI Northern Italy. Recalibrate locally set plot-level yield / N-status samples operational use. Cell granularity - finer cell_length gives denser grid risks delivery oscillations spreader; 50-100 m along -B line reasonable default 24-36 m machine. pipeline NNI - replace variability = "calibration" variability = "nni" pass NNI raster (compute_NNI_from_S2() nni_from_vi_empirical()) instead VI drive strips nitrogen status zones directly.

title: Remote Sensing Diagnosis: multi-index VIs and Nitrogen Nutrition Index
text: vignette demonstrates remote-sensing diagnosis pipeline added agrinutri 0.7.0: Compute multiple vegetation indices (VIs) multi-band raster compute_vi(). Diagnose crop nitrogen status pixel--pixel compute_NNI() / diagnose_N_status(), using species-specific critical nitrogen dilution curve Lemaire & Gastal (1997). Feed diagnosis variable-rate prescription pipeline (variable_rate_N()) applied dose responds NNI diagnosis rather raw vegetation index alone. matters: NDVI saturates LAI > 3–4. mid- late-vegetative stages (GS30+ winter wheat; V8+ maize) red-edge indices (NDRE, CIred-edge) far sensitive canopy N status. indices still just proxies: scientifically correct diagnostic variable NNI, uses dilution curve convert biomass + N% dimensionless deficiency / sufficiency index.

title: Remote Sensing Diagnosis: multi-index VIs and Nitrogen Nutrition Index
text: compute_vi() computes NDVI, NDRE, GNDVI, CIred-edge, MCARI, MSAVI2 stack, configurable band mapping. Default mapping follows Sentinel-2 L2A naming.  NDVI GNDVI typically cluster narrow range closed canopies (saturation); NDRE CIred-edge preserve variability high biomass. red-edge indices reference N diagnosis GS30+ / V8+.
code: ndvi  <- compute_vi(s2, "NDVI") ndre  <- compute_vi(s2, "NDRE") gndvi <- compute_vi(s2, "GNDVI") cire  <- compute_vi(s2, "CIred")  summary(terra::values(ndvi, mat = FALSE)) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>  0.6329  0.7314  0.7662  0.7655  0.8055  0.8615 summary(terra::values(ndre, mat = FALSE)) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>  0.1751  0.3596  0.4406  0.4456  0.5384  0.6886 par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 3)) terra::plot(ndvi,  main = "NDVI",  col = rev(terrain.colors(30))) terra::plot(ndre,  main = "NDRE",  col = rev(terrain.colors(30))) terra::plot(gndvi, main = "GNDVI", col = rev(terrain.colors(30))) terra::plot(cire,  main = "CIred", col = rev(terrain.colors(30)))

title: Remote Sensing Diagnosis: multi-index VIs and Nitrogen Nutrition Index
text: critical_N_curve() returns (, b, W_min) coefficients species-specific critical nitrogen dilution curve. Italian synonyms accepted. curve Nc = * W^(-b), Nc critical N concentration (% DM) W aboveground dry biomass (t DM / ha). Defaults come Justes 1994 (wheat), Plenet & Lemaire 1999 (maize), Sheehy 1998 (rice), Colnenne 1998 (rapeseed), Duru 1997 (grass), van Oosterom 2010 (sorghum), Debaeke 2012 (sunflower).
code: critical_N_curve("wheat") #> $a #> [1] 5.35 #>  #> $b #> [1] 0.44 #>  #> $W_min #> [1] 1.55 #>  #> $reference #> [1] "Justes et al. 1994" critical_N_curve("mais")   # italian #> $a #> [1] 3.4 #>  #> $b #> [1] 0.37 #>  #> $W_min #> [1] 1 #>  #> $reference #> [1] "Plenet & Lemaire 1999"

title: Remote Sensing Diagnosis: multi-index VIs and Nitrogen Nutrition Index
text: usual variable_rate_N() accepts normalised VI. diagnosis-guided upgrade : () use red-edge index VRT, (b) zero prescription NNI diagnosis shows excessive N status, fertiliser applied crop already -supplied.
code:
N_target <- 160   # e.g. from a preliminary N_balance()  vr <- variable_rate_N(ndre, n_dose = N_target,                       method = "holland",                       minN = 60, maxN = 200) #> Warning: [is.lonlat] unknown crs #> Warning in estimate_N_rate_from_holland_schepers(ndvi_raster = ndvi_raster, : #> Raster projection information missing. Ensure NDVI values are in 0-1 range.  # Mask out pixels classified as "excessive" (class == 3) rate_guided <- vr$rate_raster rate_guided[d$class == 3] <- 0  par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 4)) terra::plot(vr$rate_raster,      main = "VRT (NDRE + Holland)",      col  = rev(heat.colors(30))) terra::plot(rate_guided,      main = "VRT masked by NNI (class 3 -> 0)",      col  = rev(heat.colors(30))) cat("Full prescription  mean :",     round(terra::global(vr$rate_raster, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1], 1), "kg/ha
") #> Full prescription  mean : 160 kg/ha cat("NNI-guided        mean  :",     round(terra::global(rate_guided, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1], 1), "kg/ha
") #> NNI-guided        mean  : 104.5 kg/ha cat("N saved by NNI mask     :",     round(terra::global(vr$rate_raster - rate_guided, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1], 1),     "kg/ha avg, or",     round(terra::global(vr$rate_raster - rate_guided, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1] *           prod(terra::res(rate_guided)) / 10000, 1),     "kg total over the field
") #> N saved by NNI mask     : 55.5 kg/ha avg, or 55.5 kg total over the field

what: 7. Empirical NNI from a single VI raster (no GPR models)
title: Remote Sensing Diagnosis: multi-index VIs and Nitrogen Nutrition Index
text: full compute_NNI_from_S2() pipeline requires 8 pyeogpr .json model files plus 10-band Sentinel-2 L2A scene. single VI raster available (UAV NDRE, satellite NDVI, etc.), helper nni_from_vi_empirical() delivers NNI map directly published linear regression: Default slope intercept first-guess values Cao 2013 (rice), Fitzgerald 2010 Magney 2017 (wheat), Li 2014 (maize). Local recalibration 30-50 plot-level ground-truth samples strongly recommended.
code: ndre <- terra::rast("ndre_field.tif") out  <- nni_from_vi_empirical(   ndre,   index = "NDRE",       # or "NDVI", "CIred_edge"   crop  = "wheat",      # wheat / maize / rice / barley   # slope = 3.5, intercept = 0.30,  # override with local calibration   nni_thresholds = c(0.90, 1.10))  terra::plot(out$NNI,   main = "NNI (empirical)") terra::plot(out$zones, main = "Zones (1 deficient / 2 optimal / 3 excessive)")

title: Spatial Nitrogen Balance and Variable-Rate Prescription
text: vignette demonstrates full agrinutri spatial workflow: Load real soil-property rasters (bundled package) Compute spatially-explicit nitrogen balance spatial_N_balance() Generate variable-rate (VRT) prescription variable_rate_N() (Holland & Schepers method) workflow implements pipeline described Section 2.2 agrinutri SoftwareX article: field-scale balance provides regulatory-compliant N target, VRT functions redistribute space mass-balance constraint.

title: Spatial Nitrogen Balance and Variable-Rate Prescription
text: agrinutri ships six GeoTIFF rasters 12-ha arable field near Cremona (Northern Italy), ~3.5 m resolution: total nitrogen (TN, %), soil organic matter (SOM, %), clay, sand silt content (%), C/N ratio.
code: library(agrinutri) library(terra) #> terra 1.9.50  ext <- system.file("extdata", package = "agrinutri")  # Read individually: the bundled GeoTIFFs may have sub-pixel extent # mismatches from separate acquisitions, so we resample to a common # grid (the TN raster) before stacking. r_tn   <- terra::rast(file.path(ext, "Cremonesi_TN.tif")) r_som  <- terra::rast(file.path(ext, "Cremonesi_SOM.tif")) r_clay <- terra::rast(file.path(ext, "Cremonesi_Clay.tif")) r_sand <- terra::rast(file.path(ext, "Cremonesi_Sand.tif")) r_cn   <- terra::rast(file.path(ext, "Cremonesi_CNratio.tif"))  align <- function(r, ref) {   if (!terra::compareGeom(r, ref, stopOnError = FALSE)) {     r <- terra::resample(r, ref, method = "bilinear")   }   r } soil <- terra::rast(list(r_tn,                          align(r_som,  r_tn),                          align(r_clay, r_tn),                          align(r_sand, r_tn),                          align(r_cn,   r_tn))) names(soil) <- c("TN", "SOM", "Clay", "Sand", "CNratio")  soil #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 96, 101, 5  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 3.486166e-05, 3.499425e-05  (x, y) #> extent      : 9.995467, 9.998988, 45.04422, 45.04758  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) #> sources     : Cremonesi_TN.tif #>               Cremonesi_SOM.tif #>               Cremonesi_Clay.tif #>               ... and 2 more sources #> varnames    : Cremonesi_TN #>               Cremonesi_SOM #>               Cremonesi_Clay #>               Cremonesi_TN #>               Cremonesi_CNratio #> names       :  TN, SOM, Clay,      Sand, CNratio #> min values  :  ? ,  ? ,   ? ,  7.503736,      ?  #> max values  :  ? ,  ? ,   ? , 24.709644,      ? par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 4)) terra::plot(soil[["SOM"]], main = "SOM (%)", col = terrain.colors(30)) terra::plot(soil[["Clay"]], main = "Clay (%)", col = heat.colors(30))

title: Spatial Nitrogen Balance and Variable-Rate Prescription
text: spatial_N_balance() iterates N_balance() every non-NA pixel stack. Agronomic climatic parameters (crop, yield, rainfall, previous crop, organic history) uniform; spatial variability driven soil rasters alone.  field-average N apply :
code: n_map <- spatial_N_balance(   soil_stack            = soil,   expected_yield_tons_ha = 60,   crop                  = "Silage maize (class 700)",   ccp                   = "Spring-summer crop 100-130 days",   oxygen_availability   = "Normal",   winter_rain           = 160,   start_spring_rain     = 40,   prev_crop             = "Winter cereals straw removal",   source                = "Cattle slurry",   fertorg_frequency     = "every year",   location              = "Plain adjacent to urbanized areas",   forg_quantity         = 100 )  n_map #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 96, 101, 10  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 3.486166e-05, 3.499425e-05  (x, y) #> extent      : 9.995467, 9.998988, 45.04422, 45.04758  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) #> source(s)   : memory #> varnames    : Cremonesi_TN #>               Cremonesi_TN #>               Cremonesi_TN #>               Cremonesi_TN #>               Cremonesi_TN #>               ... #> names       :   A,         B,       C1, C2,         D, E, ... #> min values  : 234, 31.847374, 0.473399,  0, 19.554212, 0, ... #> max values  : 234, 35.605838, 0.504546,  0, 20.681751, 0, ... terra::plot(n_map[["N_to_apply"]],      main = "Mineral N to apply (kg N/ha)",      col = rev(terrain.colors(30))) terra::global(n_map[["N_to_apply"]], "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1] #> [1] 27.17487

title: Spatial Nitrogen Balance and Variable-Rate Prescription
text: real application NDVI raster comes UAV satellite imagery. simulate one correlated SOM (higher SOM → better canopy vigor):
code: set.seed(42) som_vals <- terra::values(soil[["SOM"]], mat = FALSE) som_01   <- (som_vals - min(som_vals, na.rm = TRUE)) /             diff(range(som_vals, na.rm = TRUE)) ndvi_vals <- 0.52 + 0.25 * som_01 + rnorm(length(som_01), 0, 0.025) ndvi_vals <- pmin(pmax(ndvi_vals, 0.35), 0.85) ndvi_vals[is.na(som_vals)] <- NA  ndvi <- terra::rast(soil[["SOM"]]) terra::values(ndvi) <- ndvi_vals names(ndvi) <- "NDVI"

title: Spatial Nitrogen Balance and Variable-Rate Prescription
text: VRT function redistributes field-mean N target across NDVI-based vigor gradient, mass-balance constraint described Section 2.2 article:
code: N_target <- terra::global(n_map[["N_to_apply"]], "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]  vr <- variable_rate_N(   ndvi_raster = ndvi,   n_dose      = N_target,   method      = "holland",   minN        = 40,   maxN        = 180 ) #> Warning: The field mean (40.0 kg/ha) cannot reach the target (27.2 kg/ha) #> within the dose bounds [40, 180].  rx <- vr$rate_raster par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 4)) terra::plot(ndvi, main = "Synthetic NDVI", col = rev(terrain.colors(30))) terra::plot(rx,   main = "VRT N prescription (kg N/ha)",      col = rev(heat.colors(30)))

title: Nutrient Balances and Variable-Rate Fertilisation Planning
text: agrinutri R package nitrogen, phosphorus potassium fertilisation planning field tree crops nutrient balance methods. Every coefficient editable data table, balance can re-parameterised regional guidelines. default parameterisation implements balance method (Annex 2) standard-dose method Emilia-Romagna Integrated Production Guidelines (Disciplinari di Produzione Integrata, DPI 2026) follows regional reference tool Fert_Office v1.26. top regulatory balance provides farm pixel-level balances, Sentinel-2 remote-sensing diagnosis (vegetation indices, Gaussian-process canopy traits, Nitrogen Nutrition Index) variable-rate prescriptions keep field mean equal compliant balance dose, exported tractor formats. coefficient tables ordinary R datasets (uptake_table, mas.table, coef_time, …), balance can inspected, versioned re-parameterized guidelines.

code: library(agrinutri)  bal <- N_balance(   expected_yield_tons_ha = 6, crop = "Grano duro (pianta intera)",   ccp = "Spring-summer crop 100-130 days",   sand = 15.5, clay = 18.5, Ntot = 1.5, SOM = 2, CN = 7.73,   oxygen_availability = "Slow", winter_rain = 150, start_spring_rain = 0,   prev_crop = "Maize stalks removed", source = "None",   location = "Isolated plain", forg_quantity = 0)  bal[c("A", "B", "C1", "C2", "D", "E", "F", "G")]   # every balance term calculate_N_fertilization(bal)                      # 142.246 kg N/ha check_MAS("Grano duro (pianta intera)", 142)        # MAS 190 kg N/ha: ok  P_balance(6, "Grano duro (pianta intera)", olsen_value = 15, olsen_unit = "P2O5",           clay = 18.5, sand = 15.5, total_carbonate = 15)$P2O5_required  # 112.9 K_balance(6, "Grano duro (pianta intera)", k_value = 150, k_unit = "K2O",           clay = 18.5, sand = 15.5)$K2O_required                         # 139.4 farm <- sf::st_read(system.file("extdata/example_farm.geojson", package = "agrinutri")) farm_balance(farm)[, c("plot_id", "crop", "N_target", "MAS_ok", "N_total_kg")] s2   <- system.file("extdata/sentinel-2/S2_cerzoo_field3_20240813.tif", package = "agrinutri") bio  <- estimate_biophysical(s2, output_dir = tempdir(),                              variables = c("LAI", "Cm", "CNC_Cprot", "FVC")) nni  <- compute_NNI_from_S2(bio$LAI, bio$Cm, bio$CNC_Cprot, cnc_layer = "CNC_Cprot",                             crop = "maize", fvc = bio$FVC) field <- sf::st_read(system.file("extdata/cerzoo_field.geojson", package = "agrinutri")) rx   <- build_strip_prescription(field[field$id == 3, ], machine_width = 24,                                  variability = "nni", nni_raster = nni$NNI,                                  n_target = 200, min_dose = 160, max_dose = 240) export_prescription(rx, file.path(tempdir(), "rx.shp"), format = "shp")

title: Nitrogen Balance Calculation — N_balance
text: Calculates nitrogen balance crop DPI Emilia-Romagna 2026 balance method (Allegato 2), reproducing regional tool Fert_Office v1.26 term term. printed DPI tables Fert_Office differ, agrinutri follows Fert_Office (see vignette("agrinutri-PK--distribution")).

title: Nitrogen Balance Calculation — N_balance
code: N_balance(   expected_yield_tons_ha = 15,   crop = "Grano tenero FF (granella)",   ccp = "Spring-summer crop 100-130 days",   sand = 50,   clay = 35,   Ntot = 1.2,   SOM = 1.2,   CN = 9.5,   oxygen_availability = "Normal",   winter_rain = 160,   start_spring_rain = 40,   prev_crop = "Winter cereals straw removal",   source = "Cattle slurry",   fertorg_frequency = "every year",   location = "Plain adjacent to urbanized areas",   forg_quantity = 100,   organic_previous_year_N = 0,   soil_group = NULL,   distribution_efficiency = NULL,   soil_seeding = c("traditional", "no-till"),   greenhouse = FALSE,   E_to_D = TRUE,   n_fixation_pct = NULL )

title: Nitrogen Balance Calculation — N_balance
text: expected_yield_tons_ha Expected crop yield tons per hectare. crop Name crop. ccp Crop calendar period (e.g., "Spring-summer crop 100-130 days"). sand Percentage sand soil. clay Percentage clay soil. Ntot Total nitrogen content soil (%). SOM Soil organic matter content (%). CN Carbon nitrogen ratio soil. oxygen_availability Oxygen availability level soil (e.g., "Normal"). winter_rain Total winter rainfall (mm). start_spring_rain Rainfall start spring (mm). prev_crop Previous crop grown field. source Source organic fertilizer (e.g., "Cattle slurry"). fertorg_frequency Frequency organic fertilizer application (e.g., "every year"). location Location field relative urban areas. forg_quantity Quantity organic fertilizer applied (m3/ha t/ha, depending source). Use 0 organic application: Forg set 0 without calling organic_fertilization(). organic_previous_year_N Optional. Total N (kg/ha) organic fertilization applied previous year (source/frequency). provided, term F (residual N previous years' organic, DPI section 3.1.6) included. Default 0. soil_group Optional override DPI organic-N efficiency (texture class). NULL (default), N_balance() uses soil.group computed sand clay via calc_soil_group_and_id_rag(), current-year organic (Forg) follows texture B. distribution_efficiency Optional. "efficient", "medium", "low" (DPI distribution quality). NULL (default), N_balance() uses "medium" Forg (typical farm practice specified). Ignored Forg forg_quantity == 0. soil_seeding One "traditional" (default) "-till". "-till", soil supply B reduced 10 kg/ha (DPI Allegato 2), crops cycle shorter one year DPI allows . greenhouse Logical. TRUE, 2 kg/ha added D (DPI 2026 greenhouse factor). Default FALSE. E_to_D Logical. TRUE (default), negative E (e.g. buried stalks = -40) added D Fert_Office v1.26 sheet C&D, E output set 0. FALSE, E stays negative balance uses calculate_N_fertilization(). E counted crop phases DPI counts precession (coef_time$precession_to_count), .e. perennial crops production. n_fixation_pct Share (%) legume N demand covered biological fixation. NULL (default) uses value proposed crop (crops.table$n_fixation_pct). booked G balance positive, Fert_Office; value lower crop's default (lacking inoculation) lowers dose ceiling 120 kg N/ha.

title: Nitrogen Balance Calculation — N_balance
text: data frame containing calculated nitrogen balance components (kg/ha): : Total nitrogen demand crop (kg/ha). B: Total soil nitrogen supply, b1 + b2 - -till reduction (kg/ha). b1: Readily available mineral nitrogen (DPI B2) (kg/ha). b2: Mineralizable N soil organic matter (DPI B1) (kg/ha). C1: Nitrogen leaching loss autumn-winter (Ca) (kg/ha). C2: Nitrogen leaching loss end winter (Cb) (kg/ha). D: Nitrogen immobilization loss (kg/ha). Includes abs(E) contribution E_to_D = TRUE E < 0, +2 greenhouse = TRUE (part Fert_Office v1.26 balance sheet). E: Nitrogen previous crop residues (kg/ha). E_to_D = TRUE raw value negative, column reports 0 (moved D). F: Nitrogen previous years' organic fertilization (kg/ha). Forg: Nitrogen organic fertilizer (current year, efficient N) (kg/ha). G: Natural contributions (kg/ha): G_deposition (atmospheric deposition x time coefficient) plus G_fixation (legume N fixation). no_till_reduction: Reduction B -till seeding (kg/ha). C_tempo, N_pct, N_limit: time coefficient phase, share balance admitted phase dose ceiling (kg/ha), used calculate_N_fertilization(). surplus_pluviometrico: Logical flag (DPI 2026 standard sheet, surplus rain).

title: Nitrogen Balance Calculation — N_balance
text: nitrogen fertilization requirement (DPI formula) : N = - B + C1 + C2 + D - E - F - G, scaled N_pct, bounded ; current-year organic N Forg subtracted give mineral N (calculate_N_fertilization()).

title: agrinutri Package Data — agrinutri-data
text: datasets loaded automatically package using LazyData: true DESCRIPTION file. Soil texture grouped three DPI classes: (1) Tendenzialmente sabbioso (S, SF, FS), (2) Franco / Medio impasto (L, F, FL, FSA, FA), (3) Tendenzialmente argilloso (FLA, , AL, ). Tables character keys retain original Italian naming used Fert_Office; English aliases (*_it columns, English primary values) provided backward compatibility earlier agrinutri versions required.

title: agrinutri Package Data — agrinutri-data
text: uptake_table Crop unit absorption/asportation coefficients N, P2O5 K2O (foglio ). 247 crops v0.2.0. e.table Precessione: N kg/ha previous crop residues, legume flag Italian alias. f.table Coefficients recovery organic fertilisation applied previous years (4 matrici x 4 frequenze = 16 rows). g.table Annual N deposition (kg/ha) per location (3 rows). soil.table USDA 12 soil classes mapped DPI 3-group (ID_Rag). tri2.table USDA soil texture triangle lookup (ID_Rag clay/sand). tri3.table Simplified USDA soil texture triangle lookup. ca.table Oxygen availability -> ID_Dre mapping. cb.table Leaching C (kg/ha) immobilization factor fc_D ID_Rag x ID_Dre. coefN_readily Coefficient readily available N per soil group. coefN_mineralised Mineralisation coefficient per soil group x C/N. coef_time C_tempo time adjustment factors phase x cycle; v0.2.0 also carries DPI 2026 percentages N, P2O5 K2O allowed per phase, plus advance_allowed husbandry flags. s2.rast Example Sentinel-2 raster (5 bands) vignettes, stored terra PackedSpatRaster. Unwrap terra::rast(s2.rast) use.

title: agrinutri Package Data — agrinutri-data
text: mas.table Maximum allowed doses (MAS) per crop (DPI 2026, RR 2/2024); includes standard N dose, MAS_N, max_increment, max_N_dose. crops.table Crop master list genus/species, N fixation % no_till_reduction flag (foglio Coltura). crop_groups.table 6 crop macro-groups: arboree, erbacee, foraggere, orticole, da_seme, baby_life. texture_groups.table Texture grouping specific_weight, P immobilisation factor soil weight 20/30/40/50 cm. .table, so_max_input SOM class (12) maximum annual input (t ss/ha) per class. ph.table Soil pH classes (7). total_carbonate.table, active_carbonate.table Total active carbonate classes soil reactivity. p_availability.table, p_availability_meta Olsen-P availability classes P <-> P2O5 conversion + P immobilisation factor. k_availability.table Exchangeable-K availability classes per texture grouping. fertilizer_types.table Fertiliser type classification (11 classes). organic_fertilizers.table 21 organic matrices ss, N, P2O5, K2O (min/avg/max), zootec flag, increment. efficiency.table DPI 2026 organic N efficiency: ID_Rag x level x sector x dose (220 rows). distribution_modalities.table 22 distribution modalities (epoch + technique). cycle_modality.table Compatibility matrix crop-cycle x distribution modality x efficiency level. cycles.table, cycle_phases.table Crop cycles (6) phase-duration (17). c_d.table Combined C (leaching) fc_D (immobilisation) lookup (foglio C&D Fert_Office v1.26).

title: Build a strip-by-strip prescription map from a field polygon — build_strip_prescription
text: field sf POLYGON (single feature) field boundary. machine_width Numeric, working width spreader / spray boom metres (default 24). cell_length Optional numeric. supplied >0, every strip subdivided rectangular cells length (metres) along -B direction, producing true 2-D prescription grid. NULL 0, strip left single polygon (classic "strip map"). angle_deg Optional numeric. Azimuth -B line degrees (0 = east, 90 = north). Overrides ab_line supplied. ab_line Optional sf LINESTRING giving driving direction. ab_line angle_deg NULL, long side field used. variability One "uniform", "calibration", "nni", "classes". vi_raster terra::SpatRaster vegetation index (0-1); legacy raster object accepted converted terra::rast(). Required "calibration" "classes". nni_raster , NNI values. Required "nni". n_target Target field-level mean dose (kg N ha\(^{-1}\)). min_dose, max_dose Numeric caps (kg N ha\(^{-1}\)). vi_low, vi_high Two-point calibration anchors (variability = "calibration"). calibration_inverse = TRUE (default), vi_low dose capped max_dose; vi_high min_dose. FALSE, vi_low dose capped min_dose; vi_high max_dose. calibration_inverse Logical. TRUE (default), NDVI dose inversely related along segment (vi_low \(\rightarrow\) max_dose). FALSE, NDVI dose increase together (vi_low \(\rightarrow\) min_dose). Applies "calibration" dose ordering "classes". thr_lo, thr_hi NNI thresholds (variability = "nni"). n_classes Integer number equal-spaced dose classes variability = "classes" (default 5). preserve_mean Logical. TRUE (default) strip- level dose rescaled area-weighted mean matches n_target. Guarantees mass-balance compliance balance-based field ceiling. crs_metric EPSG code metric CRS strips drawn. NULL (default) uses WGS 84 / UTM zone field centroid, machine_width, cell_length area_ha true ground distances areas. (Web Mercator, EPSG:3857, suitable: 45 degrees latitude shrinks 24 m width 17 m ground.)

title: Build a strip-by-strip prescription map from a field polygon — build_strip_prescription
text: sf object strip polygons columns strip_id, dose (kg N ha\(^{-1}\)), area_ha, mean_vi mean_nni available. CRS matches input.

title: Build a strip-by-strip prescription map from a field polygon — build_strip_prescription
text: builder works entirely metric CRS (Web Mercator default); final sf object returned original CRS input field downstream tools see consistent coordinates.

title: Build a strip-by-strip prescription map from a field polygon — build_strip_prescription
text: "uniform" Every strip receives n_target dose. Useful baseline. "calibration" Samples mean vi_raster value per strip maps dose via two-point linear curve vi_low vi_high. calibration_inverse = TRUE (default), higher VI implies lower dose (typical side-dress). FALSE, higher VI implies higher dose. "nni" Samples mean nni_raster value per strip translates three agronomic zones Lemaire & Gastal: deficient (NNI < thr_lo) gets max_dose, optimal (thr_lo <= NNI <= thr_hi) gets n_target, excessive (NNI > thr_hi) gets min_dose. "classes" Splits strips n_classes NDVI quantiles assigns increasing decreasing dose ladder consistent calibration_inverse: TRUE, lowest VI class gets max_dose; FALSE, gets min_dose. Regardless method, mean dose across field rescaled match n_target (mass-balance constraint) preserve_mean = TRUE (default).

title: Build a strip-by-strip prescription map from a field polygon — build_strip_prescription
text: ab_line NULL, -B direction taken longest edge polygon's minimum-area bounding rectangle (via sf::st_minimum_rotated_rectangle()). typically recovers "long side" convention farmers use field. ab_line sf LINESTRING, first segment defines driving direction.

title: Calculate Nitrogen Fertilization Requirement — calculate_N_fertilization
text: function calculates mineral nitrogen apply nitrogen balance components, Fert_Office v1.26 : balance   multiplied share admitted crop phase (N_pct; 0 planting, 1 phases), bounded 0 crop's ceiling (N_limit, usually 340 kg N/ha), current-year organic N Forg subtracted (result never negative):   : : Crop nitrogen demand B: Soil nitrogen supply C1, C2: Leaching losses D: Immobilization losses E: Nitrogen previous crop residues F: Nitrogen previous years' organic fertilization (0 balance) Forg: Nitrogen organic fertilizer (current year) G: Natural nitrogen contribution
code: N = A - B + C1 + C2 + D - E - F - G N_fert = max(0, min(max(0, N * N_pct), N_limit) - Forg)

Useful custom local calibration. is_percent Logical. N_content supplied percentage (e.g. 2.5 2.5pct) rather fraction? Default FALSE (fraction). Auto-detected warned values > 1.

code: compute_NNI_from_S2(   lai_rast,   cm_rast,   cnc_rast,   cnc_layer = c("CNC_Cprot", "CNC_Cab"),   crop,   params = NULL,   fvc = NULL,   scl = NULL,   scl_keep = c(4L, 5L, 6L, 7L),   nni_thresholds = c(0.9, 1.1),   return_intermediates = TRUE )

title: End-to-end Nitrogen Nutrition Index pipeline from Sentinel-2 L2A — compute_NNI_from_S2
text: lai_rast SpatRaster path LAI layer produced estimate_biophysical. cm_rast SpatRaster path Cm layer. cnc_rast SpatRaster path canopy N layer. cnc_layer Character. Either "CNC_Cprot" (default) "CNC_Cab". Controls conversion applied. crop Character. Crop name, resolved via crop_params_NNI. params Optional list overriding defaults returned crop_params_NNI (e.g. locally calibrated alpha_leaf k_NChl). fvc SpatRaster (path) fractional vegetation cover, optional. provided pipeline drops pixels FVC < params$fvc_min. scl SpatRaster (path) Sentinel-2 SCL layer, optional. Pixels scl_keep masked. scl_keep Integer vector SCL classes keep (default c(4, 5, 6, 7) = VEGETATION, NOT_VEGETATED, WATER, UNCLASSIFIED). nni_thresholds Numeric length-2 vector lower upper NNI thresholds (default c(0.90, 1.10)). return_intermediates Logical. TRUE returned list also contains intermediate W, N_total N_actual rasters.

title: End-to-end Nitrogen Nutrition Index pipeline from Sentinel-2 L2A — compute_NNI_from_S2
text: named list SpatRaster layers: W (t DM ha\(^{-1}\)) – aboveground biomass N_actual (pct DM) – plant N concentration N_crit (pct DM) – critical N dilution curve NNI – Nitrogen Nutrition Index (dimensionless) zones – integer raster (1 deficient / 2 optimal / 3 excessive) mask – logical raster retained pixels Returned items NULL return_intermediates = FALSE intermediate variable requested.

title: End-to-end Nitrogen Nutrition Index pipeline from Sentinel-2 L2A — compute_NNI_from_S2
text: pipeline implements classical Lemaire & Gastal (1997) formulation: $$W_{leaf} = LAI \cdot C_m \cdot 10^4  \quad (\mathrm{g\ m^{-2}})$$ $$W = W_{leaf} / \alpha_{leaf}  \quad (\mathrm{g\ m^{-2}})$$ $$N_{total} = k \cdot CNC\_Cab  \quad \mathrm{}  \quad N_{total} = CNC\_Cprot$$ $$N_{actual}(\%) = 100 \cdot N_{total} / W$$ $$N_c(\%) = \cdot (W_{tha})^{-b}$$ $$NNI = N_{actual} / N_c$$ \(\alpha_{leaf}\) leaf--total aboveground allocation coefficient \(k\) N--chlorophyll ratio (crop-specific, see crop_params_NNI). \(W_{tha}\) W rescaled t DM ha\(^{-1}\). Two N-content pathways supported: Protein path (cnc_layer = "CNC_Cprot", default). Uses GPR retrieval trained canopy N protein content directly — internally consistent path, extra coefficient needed. Chlorophyll path (cnc_layer = "CNC_Cab"). Uses canopy chlorophyll retrieval multiplies canopy-level N:Chl ratio \(k\) (default ~55-60, requires local calibration — see crop_params_NNI). Preferred CNC_Cab best-trained model target crop calibration work already done.

title: End-to-end Nitrogen Nutrition Index pipeline from Sentinel-2 L2A — compute_NNI_from_S2
text: Two masks applied NNI computation: fvc raster supplied, pixels FVC < crop_params$fvc_min removed (default threshold 0.50). level BRDF contaminated soil background GPR retrievals degrade. Pixels W crop_params$w_min masked critical-N dilution curve defined seedling stage (default 1 t DM ha\(^{-1}\)). Optional Sentinel-2 SCL (Scene Classification Layer) classes can dropped via scl_keep (vector valid classes; defaults standard vegetation-safe classes 4, 5, 6, 7 = VEGETATION, NOT_VEGETATED, WATER, UNCLASSIFIED).

title: End-to-end Nitrogen Nutrition Index pipeline from Sentinel-2 L2A — compute_NNI_from_S2
text: NNI discretised three classes following Lemaire & Gastal (1997): Thresholds user-configurable via nni_thresholds argument.

title: End-to-end Nitrogen Nutrition Index pipeline from Sentinel-2 L2A — compute_NNI_from_S2
text: Lemaire G, Gastal F. N uptake distribution plant canopies. : Diagnosis Nitrogen Status Crops, Springer, 1997. Houles V, Guerif M, Mary B. Elaboration nitrogen nutrition indicator winter wheat based leaf area index chlorophyll content. Eur J Agron 2007;27:1-11.

text: stack terra::SpatRaster required spectral bands (legacy raster object accepted converted terra::rast()). Band names (layer indices) mapped bands. index One "NDVI", "NDRE", "GNDVI", "CIred", "MCARI", "MSAVI2" (case-insensitive). bands Named list character vector mapping index inputs (red, red_edge, nir, green) layer names stack. Defaults Sentinel-2 L2A naming (red="B04", red_edge="B05", nir="B08", green="B03"). bands required chosen index looked . scale_factor Numeric. input reflectance stored integer DN (e.g. Sentinel-2 L2A 0–10000), divide factor computing index. Default 1 (reflectance already 0–1). clamp Logical. TRUE (default bounded indices NDVI, NDRE, GNDVI, MSAVI2), clamp output range -1 1. Ignored CIred MCARI (unbounded).

title: Compute a vegetation index from a multi-band raster — compute_vi

title: Compute a vegetation index from a multi-band raster — compute_vi
text: Index formulas (references References section): NDVI (NIR minus Red) divided (NIR plus Red). Rouse 1974. NDRE (NIR minus RedEdge) divided (NIR plus RedEdge). Gitelson Merzlyak 1994. GNDVI (NIR minus Green) divided (NIR plus Green). Gitelson 1996. CIred NIR divided RedEdge, minus one. Gitelson 2003. MCARI quantity RedEdge minus Red minus 0.2 times quantity RedEdge minus Green, multiplied ratio RedEdge Red. Daughtry 2000. MSAVI2 2 NIR + 1 minus square root (2 NIR + 1)^2 minus 8 times NIR minus Red, divided two. Qi 1994. NDVI saturates LAI > 3–4 closed canopies; mid- late-vegetative stages (GS30+ cereals, V8+ maize) red-edge indices (NDRE, CIred) considerably sensitive canopy nitrogen status (Clarke 2001; Li 2014; Cao 2015). agrinutri variable-rate functions (variable_rate_N(), estimate_N_rate_from_calibration_curve(), estimate_N_rate_from_holland_schepers()) accept normalised VI 0–1 scale, user can substitute NDVI NDRE GNDVI transparently.

Photochem. Photobiol. B 22. Gitelson, .. et al. (1996). Use green channel remote sensing global vegetation EOS-MODIS. Remote Sens. Environ. 58, 289-298. Gitelson, .. et al. (2003). Relationships leaf chlorophyll content spectral reflectance. J. Plant Physiol. 160, 271-282. Daughtry, C.S.T. et al. (2000). Estimating corn leaf chlorophyll concentration leaf canopy reflectance. Remote Sens. Environ. 74. Qi, J. et al. (1994). modified soil adjusted vegetation index. Remote Sens. Environ. 48, 119-126. Clarke, T.R. et al. (2001). Remote sensing nitrogen status wheat. Proc. Beltwide Cotton Conf. Li, F. et al. (2014). Improving estimation summer maize nitrogen status red edge-based spectral vegetation indices. F. Crops Res. 157. Cao, Q. et al. (2015). Active canopy sensing winter wheat nitrogen status: evaluation two sensor systems. Comput. Electron. Agric. 112.

title: Crop-specific parameters for the Nitrogen Nutrition Index pipeline — crop_params_NNI
text: dilution-curve coefficients b well established listed crops across European cropping systems; rarely need recalibration. alpha_leaf k_NChl two locally sensitive parameters. -calibrated values commonly introduce 15-30pct bias final NNI map. minimal calibration dataset consists 30-50 plot-level samples across growing season, analysed dry biomass (oven 65 degC) total plant N (Kjeldahl Dumas), paired matching Sentinel-2 acquisition date. NNI meaningful inside crop-specific phenological windows (e.g. GS31-GS55 wheat, V6-V12 maize). Outside windows critical-N curve valid. scene dominated partially covered pixels (FVC < 0.5), GPR retrievals degrade soil signal enters BRDF. Use fvc_min prune .

title: GPR-based estimation of canopy biophysical variables from Sentinel-2 L2A — estimate_biophysical
text: function pure-R port pyeogpr inference pipeline (Estevez et al., 2022). depends terra (raster /O) jsonlite (model loading) produces numerical output reference Python implementation machine precision (correlation 1.0, relative error < 1.4 \(\cdot 10^{-8}\) 200-pixel benchmark). models trained PROSAIL + canopy N simulations distributed *.json files.

title: GPR-based estimation of canopy biophysical variables from Sentinel-2 L2A — estimate_biophysical
text: S2 raster expected store surface reflectance scaled scale (default 10000), .e. reflectance = DN / scale 0-1.5 range. "harmonized" / offset-applied convention shared compute_vi, matches bundled example scenes analysis-ready L2A products (Copernicus harmonized, Google Earth Engine HARMONIZED, sen2r), reflectance range bundled GPR models trained (per-band training means 0.04-0.41). Accordingly additive offset applied default (apply_offset = FALSE). raw Processing Baseline 04.00+ L2A DN, BOA_ADD_OFFSET -1000 yet applied, set apply_offset = TRUE (offset = -1000) function computes reflectance = (DN + offset) / scale. Getting wrong shifts every band ~0.1 reflectance can drive pixels valid range, case GPR returns empty (-NA) maps; function warns valid pixels fall outside 0-1.5. One GeoTIFF written per requested variable (plus _unc.tif file prediction standard deviation variables whose model exposes pre-computed Linv_pre_calc matrix). Output rasters inherit geometry (CRS, extent, resolution) input.

title: GPR-based estimation of canopy biophysical variables from Sentinel-2 L2A — estimate_biophysical

title: Leaching Loss of Nitrogen — leaching_loss
text: Let \(N_p\) leachable N pronto: b1 crops cycle shorter one year, fixed 30 kg N/ha perennial crops production (perennial = TRUE, .e. time coefficient 1). C1 (\(C_a\), autumn–winter) Depends winter rainfall \(y\) (1 October – 31 January, winter_rain, mm): \(N_p \times \min(\max(y - 150, 0), 100)/100\), .e. loss 150 mm whole pool 250 mm. 0 autumn_loss = FALSE (first phase crop cycle, e.g. second crop pre-planting, Fert_Office). C2 (\(C_b\), end winter) \(s = y + f - 250\), \(f\) February rainfall (start_spring_rain): \(s > 0\) N pronto yet lost (\(N_p - C_a\)) lost, plus 1 kg N/ha every 10 mm \(s\) \(y > 150\) mm. oxygen_availability validated ca.table consistency balance terms; leaching formulas use .

title: Calculate soil fertility parameters (B = B1 + B2 in DPI). — soil_fertility
text: Ntot Total nitrogen content soil (g/kg, per mille). SOM Soil organic matter content (%). soil.group Soil group (e.g., "Sandy textures"). CN Carbon--nitrogen ratio. ccp Crop category planting period (e.g., "Autumn-winter crop <150 days"). soil_seeding Seeding mode, one "traditional" (default) "-till". crop Optional crop name; used check whether -till reduction applies crop. NULL, reduction applies every crop. coefN_readily, coefN_mineralised, coef_time Lookup tables.

title: Calculate soil fertility parameters (B = B1 + B2 in DPI). — soil_fertility
text: named list containing: b1: Readily available nitrogen (kg/ha), DPI B2 (0 perennial crops production). b2: Mineralized nitrogen SOM (kg/ha), DPI B1. b1_potential: N pronto perennial rule (used leaching term). no_till_reduction: Reduction -till seeding (kg/ha). B: Total soil supply b1 + b2 - no_till_reduction (kg/ha). C_tempo: Time coefficient crop phase. units: units output values ("kg/ha").

title: Calculate soil fertility parameters (B = B1 + B2 in DPI). — soil_fertility
text: b1 = coef.N.readily x min(Ntot, 2.1); counted crops time coefficient 1 (cycle shorter one year). Perennial crops production (C_tempo = 1) use B = b2 . b2 = coef.N.mineralised x min(SOM, 3) x C_tempo; DPI keeps mineralised N constant 3 percent organic matter. soil_seeding = "-till" (semina su sodo) soil supply reduced 10 kg N/ha, crops DPI allows (crops.table$no_till_reduction) b1 counted. Total B = b1 + b2 - no_till_reduction.

title: Build an agrinutri soil input stack from SoilGrids (open global default) — soilgrids_input
text: aoi Area interest: sf/sfc object, terra::SpatVector, path vector file readable terra::vect. extent (buffered) downloaded. depths Character vector SoilGrids depth intervals combine thickness-weighted topsoil value. Defaults 0 30 cm topsoil (c("0-5", "5-15", "15-30")). Accepted: "0-5", "5-15", "15-30", "30-60", "60-100", "100-200". crs_out Target coordinate reference system returned stack (anything terra::crs accepts). Defaults CRS aoi (template supplied). template Optional terra::SpatRaster whose grid output resampled (alignment field raster). Note resampling 250 m product finer grid add spatial detail. uncertainty Logical; TRUE, also download Q0.05 Q0.95 quantiles append per-property standard-deviation layers (Clay_sd, Sand_sd, TN_sd, SOM_sd, approximated (Q0.95 - Q0.05) / 3.29 converted units) use input error Monte-Carlo propagation. buffer Numeric buffer (metres) added around AOI extent cropping, edge pixels lost. Default 500.

title: Build an agrinutri soil input stack from SoilGrids (open global default) — soilgrids_input
text: terra::SpatRaster layers TN (g/kg), SOM (percent), Clay (percent), Sand (percent) CNratio (dimensionless), masked aoi crs_out; plus four *_sd layers uncertainty = TRUE. result ready pass soil_stack argument spatial_N_balance().

title: Build an agrinutri soil input stack from SoilGrids (open global default) — soilgrids_input
text: SoilGrids 250 m global product modest local accuracy (global cross-validation model efficiency 0.5 total nitrogen 0.65 organic carbon), drives field-mean regulatory dose farm total, within-field 10 m pattern. Treat open default benchmark value local sampling, validated field input. Unit conversions applied raw SoilGrids values (returned geodata): clay sand g/kg percent (divide 10); total nitrogen cg/kg g/kg (divide 100); organic carbon dg/kg g/kg (divide 10); soil organic matter organic-carbon percent times 1.724; carbon--nitrogen ratio organic carbon total nitrogen (g/kg).

title: Variable-rate nitrogen from balance + NDVI — variable_rate_N
text: Bridges constant-rate output N_balance() / calculate_N_fertilization() scheda_N() spatial NDVI-based variable-rate estimators agrinutri (estimate_N_rate_from_calibration_curve() estimate_N_rate_from_holland_schepers()).

title: Variable-rate nitrogen from balance + NDVI — variable_rate_N
code: variable_rate_N(   ndvi_raster,   n_dose,   method = c("calibration", "holland"),   envelope = 0.25,   minN = NULL,   maxN = NULL,   mas_cap = NULL,   plot = FALSE )

title: Variable-rate nitrogen from balance + NDVI — variable_rate_N
text: ndvi_raster terra::SpatRaster NDVI (0–1); layer NDVI present, otherwise first layer. Legacy raster objects accepted converted terra::rast(). n_dose Numeric. Field-average N dose (kg/ha) N_balance() + calculate_N_fertilization(), scheda_N()$dose_final, custom target. method Either "calibration" (default, two-point linear) "holland" (Holland & Schepers sufficiency index). envelope Numeric (0, 1). Half-amplitude dose range around n_dose calibration method. Default 0.25 (.e. minN = 0.75 * n_dose, maxN = 1.25 * n_dose). minN, maxN Optional explicit override envelope (kg/ha). given, also bound per-pixel rates Holland-Schepers method mass-balance rescaling. mas_cap Numeric NULL. provided, caps per-pixel rate never exceeds MAS limit (e.g. get_MAS()). plot Logical, passed underlying estimator. Default FALSE.

title: Variable-rate nitrogen from balance + NDVI — variable_rate_N
text: list : rate_raster terra::SpatRaster N rate per pixel (kg/ha). mean_kg_ha Mean rate non-NA pixels (kg/ha). min_kg_ha, max_kg_ha Min max rate non-NA pixels. n_dose_input input field-average N dose. method method used.

title: Variable-rate nitrogen from balance + NDVI — variable_rate_N
text: Two integration patterns supported: Calibration curve (method = "calibration"): agronomic balance determines target field-average dose; function derives minN/maxN envelope around (default +/- 25%) applies linear NDVI-driven calibration (low NDVI = N, high NDVI = less N). Holland & Schepers (method = "holland"): agronomic balance used base N rate H&S sufficiency-index algorithm. output preserves field-average dose computed balance: raster variable rates mean equal input n_dose (water-filling rescaling within ), agronomic constraint (MAS, ZVN) kept.

title: Variable-rate nitrogen from balance + NDVI — variable_rate_N
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(terra) library(agrinutri) # NDVI raster data(s2.rast) ndvi <- terra::rast(s2.rast)   # s2.rast is a PackedSpatRaster; unwrap it  # 1) Compute agronomic dose with the balance bal <- N_balance(expected_yield_tons_ha = 6,                  crop = "Grano duro (pianta intera)",                  ccp  = "Spring-summer crop 100-130 days",                  sand = 15.5, clay = 18.5,                  Ntot = 1.5, SOM = 2, CN = 7.73,                  oxygen_availability = "Normal",                  winter_rain = 150, start_spring_rain = 0,                  prev_crop = "Maize stalks removed",                  source = "None", fertorg_frequency = "every year",                  location = "Plain adjacent to urbanized areas",                  forg_quantity = 0) n_dose <- calculate_N_fertilization(bal)   # ~128 kg/ha  # 2) Spatialise via NDVI calibration vr <- variable_rate_N(ndvi, n_dose = n_dose, method = "calibration",                       mas_cap = get_MAS("Grano duro (pianta intera)")$mas_N) terra::plot(vr$rate_raster) vr$mean_kg_ha } # }
